frames.narration: Without a CDN, a user in Tokyo talks to the origin in the US directly. The round trip is long every single time.
Add a CDN. A nearby edge server now sits between them, and the user is routed to it.
First request in the region. The edge is close (about 15 ms), but it has nothing yet: a cache miss.
The edge fetches the file from the origin once, the slow way.
It returns the file to the user and keeps a copy for a day. This first user paid the full price.
The next user in Tokyo asks for the same file.
The edge answers from its copy in about 15 ms. The origin is not involved at all.
When the file changes, either purge it from the edges or publish it under a new URL (logo.v2.jpg) so no old copy can be served.
